title: "Radius Neighbors Regression"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

## Overview

This example demonstrates radius neighbors regression using the `aoclda` package.

```{r library}
library(aoclda)
```

## Define Data

```{r data}
x_train <- matrix(
   c(
      -1, -2, -3, 1, 2, 3,
      -1, -1, -2, 3, 5, -1,
      2, 3, -1, 1, 1, 2
   ),
   nrow = 6, ncol = 3
)
y_train <- c(1.5, 2.3, 0.6, 1, 2.8, 5.2)

x_test <- matrix(
   c(
      -2, -1, 2,
      2, -2, 1,
      3, -1, -3
   ),
   nrow = 3, ncol = 3
)
```

## Fit and Query

```{r rnn}
rnn <- nearest_neighbors$new(radius = 3.0, outlier_handling = -1.0)
rnn$fit(x_train, y_train)

rn_result <- rnn$radius_neighbors(x_test,
   radius = 2.0,
   return_distance = TRUE, sort_results = FALSE
)
y_test <- rnn$regressor_predict(x_test, search_mode = "radius_neighbors")
```

## Results

```{r results}
cat("Indices of the nearest neighbors:\n")
print(lapply(rn_result, function(e) e$indices))

cat("\nCorresponding distances of the nearest neighbors:\n")
print(lapply(rn_result, function(e) e$distances))

cat("\nPredicted targets for the test data matrix:\n")
print(y_test)
```
